results_summary: The paper demonstrates that integrating DiskANN into Azure Cosmos DB achieves approximately 20ms query latency at 10 million vector scale while offering 43× lower query cost than Pinecone and 12× lower than Zilliz serverless enterprise products. The system maintains stable recall over long update sequences without requiring index rebuilds or merges, and scales out to billions of vectors via automatic partitioning. Query cost increases less than 2× despite a 100× increase in index size per partition, and dimensionality increases have minimal cost impact. The design eliminates data replication between an operational database and a separate vector database while inheriting Cosmos DB's high availability, durability, and multi-tenant cost structures.

title: WoW: A Window-to-Window Incremental Index for Range-Filtering Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is a new indexing method (WoW) for approximate nearest neighbor search with range filtering in vector databases, including its design, theoretical analysis, and benchmarking against existing RFANNS indices. It is squarely about vector database core technology.
research_focus: Designing a dedicated index for range-filtering approximate nearest neighbor search (RFANNS) in vector databases that supports fully incremental construction and handles arbitrary range filters with varying query selectivity and correlation.
method: The paper proposes WoW, a window graph-based RFANNS index that builds hierarchical window graphs with varying window sizes using a Window-Based Tree (WBT) for incremental insertion. For querying, it employs query selectivity to select the most relevant window graphs and combines multiple window graphs to recover missing edges relative to the oracle proximity graph. Theoretical analysis provides time complexity bounds and optimal parameter settings.
indexing_methods: window graph; hierarchical window graphs; oracle proximity graph; RNG (Relative Neighbor Graph); hashing-based ANNS; partition-based ANNS; graph-based ANNS; WBT (Window-Based Tree)
application_domain: Vector database management systems; examples include e-commerce image search with price filtering and medical RAG question answering with age-range filtering
results_summary: The paper proposes WoW, a fully incremental window graph-based index for RFANNS, and evaluates it against existing baselines on real-world datasets. For index construction, WoW's indexing time is on par with the most building-efficient baseline and 4.9× faster than the most query-efficient index (DIGRA) while being 0.4-0.5× smaller in size. For RFANNS queries, WoW is 4× faster than the best incremental index and 1.5× faster than the best statically-built index on high-selectivity workloads, with equal or better performance on other workloads. The paper also proves that insertion time complexity is O(log²n) and query time complexity is O(log n'), matching the oracle RNG bound.
limitations: The index only supports single-attribute range filtering, not multi-attribute filtering; In-place update and deletion of existing entries are not yet supported
research_gaps: Extending WoW to multi-attribute range filtering; Adding in-place update and deletion support to WoW

title: Elastic Index Selection for Label-Hybrid AKNN Search
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is vector indexing and approximate nearest neighbor search with label constraints, proposing a new index-selection strategy (EIS) that is core vector database technology. It directly addresses how to build and select indexes for efficient similarity search, which is the central concern of vector databases.
research_focus: Selecting which label sets to index for label-hybrid approximate k-nearest neighbor (AKNN) search in order to balance storage space and query efficiency, formalized as the Elastic Index Selection (EIS) problem.
method: Formalizing the EIS problem as a constrained optimization, proving its NP-completeness, and proposing greedy algorithms for an efficiency-constrained variant (minimizing index space under a lower bound on the elastic factor) and a space-constrained variant (maximizing the elastic factor under a fixed space budget). The approach is index-agnostic and leverages label-containment relationships to share indexes across query-label sets.
application_domain: E-commerce product search, recommendation systems, face recognition, text retrieval, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for large language models
results_summary: The paper formalizes the Elastic Index Selection (EIS) problem for label-hybrid AKNN search, proves it is NP-complete, and proposes greedy algorithms for two optimization variants. Extensive experiments on SIFT, MSMARCO, and OpenAI-1536 datasets demonstrate 10x-800x speedups over state-of-the-art techniques such as UNG and ACORN. At 95% recall with |Σ|=12, ELI-0.2 achieves a 4x speedup over UNG on SIFT and a 10x speedup on MSMARCO, while maintaining stable performance as |Σ| grows to 32. In contrast, UNG's efficiency degrades sharply with increasing alphabet size, and ACORN plateaus in accuracy for large |Σ| due to limitations in its PreFiltering strategy. The proposed method is index-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into existing vector database systems.
limitations: In extreme cases where query-label sets are completely disjoint with no containment relationship, index sharing becomes ineffective, forcing either high space cost or a small elastic factor.; A modest performance gap exists between ELI-0.2 and ELI-2.0, with ELI-0.2 often performing slightly better because ELI-2.0's elastic factor drops below 0.2 for large alphabet sizes under Zipf distributions.
research_gaps: Hardware acceleration for further speedups is identified as future work.

title: Accelerating Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in Hierarchical Graphs: Efficient Level Navigation with Shortcuts
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is proposing and evaluating a new ANN index (SHG) for vector databases, directly addressing core vector database technology of vector indexing and nearest neighbor search.
research_focus: Accelerating Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search in hierarchical graph-based indexes by bypassing intermediate and redundant levels, addressing the efficiency bottleneck of exhaustive level-by-level traversals in vector databases.
method: The paper proposes SHG (Shortcut-enabled Hierarchical Graph), which combines a hierarchical vector compression method to reduce distance computation time across levels with a novel 'learned shortcut' data structure (piecewise linear models trained on k-NN density estimation samples) to infer the number of intermediate levels that can be safely skipped during search.
indexing_methods: HNSW; LSH-APG; SHG; hierarchical vector compression; graph-based indexes; tree-based indexes; hash-based indexes; quantization-based indexes
application_domain: Information retrieval and generative AI inference via vector databases
results_summary: The paper proposes the SHG index and evaluates it against state-of-the-art methods on eight benchmark datasets. SHG achieves a 1.5-1.8× speedup over existing methods while maintaining the same search accuracy, with only 3 MB additional memory overhead for storing shortcuts. It also demonstrates superior robustness, improving recall by up to 20% for 'unseen' query vectors compared to LSH-APG. The index handles data updates efficiently with 12 ms insertion latency while maintaining over 95% recall and 10 ms search time.
limitations: Intermediate levels in hierarchical graph-based indexes (e.g., HNSW) often involve unnecessary traversals that can be avoided; Exact distance calculations over high-dimensional vectors are computationally expensive

title: RED-ANNS: An RDMA-Enabled Distributed Framework for Graph-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is the core technology of vector databases—specifically distributed graph-based ANNS indexing and search—proposing a new system architecture, analyzing the limitations of existing vector databases like Milvus, and benchmarking against them.
research_focus: The paper addresses the resource inefficiency of existing distributed ANNS solutions that rely on segmentation-based (MapReduce-style) approaches, and proposes a new RDMA-enabled distributed framework (RED-ANNS) that maintains a logically full graph index across multiple nodes for more efficient large-scale vector search.
method: RED-ANNS uses an RDMA network to create a shared memory space across multiple nodes, maintains a full Vamana/DiskANN graph index spanning all nodes, and employs locality-aware data placement, affinity-based query scheduling, and a dependency-relaxed best-first search algorithm with data prefetching to reduce and hide remote access overhead.
indexing_methods: HNSW; Vamana; DiskANN; Inverted file indexing; Quantization; Best-First Search; k-means
application_domain: Large-scale in-memory vector search for retrieval-augmented generation, recommendation systems, search engines, and intelligent question answering
results_summary: The paper identifies that existing distributed ANNS solutions suffer significant performance degradation (2.1× to 2.9×) as the number of data segments increases, due to loss of graph connectivity and increased distance calculations. RED-ANNS avoids this by maintaining a full graph index across a shared RDMA memory space, reducing remote accesses through locality-aware placement and affinity-based scheduling, and hiding latency via a dependency-relaxed best-first search with prefetching. Experiments on 100M-scale datasets demonstrate up to 2.5× performance improvement over MapReduce-style distributed approaches and up to 5.3× over open-source vector databases. The paper also shows that probing only a subset of segments can severely hurt recall, particularly on datasets with dispersed ground-truth distributions.

title: LSMDiskANN: Update-friendly Disk-resident Vector Index Framework
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is a novel disk-resident vector index framework (LSMDiskANN) that directly proposes and evaluates improvements to vector indexing technology, including index architecture design, compaction strategies, and performance under mixed workloads.
research_focus: How to efficiently support large-scale vector updates in disk-based vector indexes while maintaining high query performance under mixed query-update workloads.
method: Proposes LSMDiskANN, an LSM-inspired (log-structured merge) disk-resident vector index framework built on the FreshDiskANN architecture. Introduces a three-level structure with a disk intermediate layer, a dynamic parameter selection mechanism for disk component search, and a relayout strategy for the deletion phase of compaction to reduce query latency and I/O overhead during merges.
application_domain: Large-scale high-dimensional vector search in vector databases, particularly in the context of large language models
results_summary: The paper proposes LSMDiskANN, an LSM-inspired update-friendly disk-based vector indexing framework that introduces a disk intermediate layer, dynamic disk component search parameter selection, and a relayout algorithm for the delete phase of merge operations. Comparative experiments and ablation analyses on several classic large-scale high-dimensional vector datasets under both rapid expansion and stable update scenarios were conducted. Results show query throughput improved by up to 35.5%, update throughput by up to 14.24%, and tail query latency reduced by up to 73.45% compared to FreshDiskANN. The framework effectively enhances overall performance and stability under mixed query-update workloads.

title: Efficient Updating Method for K-nearest Neighbor Graph in Vector Databases
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is the KNN graph, a core indexing structure in vector databases, and it proposes a novel method (FastAdjust) for efficiently updating this structure, which is directly about vector database core technology.
research_focus: Efficiently updating K-nearest neighbor (KNN) graphs in vector databases when embedding models are fine-tuned, avoiding the high computational cost of full graph reconstruction.
method: FastAdjust employs a local incremental update strategy: first using a product quantization-based clustering structure to locate candidate neighbors for each data point, then adaptively allocating update resources based on data density and the magnitude of embedding variation to minimize unnecessary recomputation.
application_domain: Vector database indexing infrastructure; downstream applications include text clustering, document recommendation, GNN modeling, and large-scale document retrieval/recommendation systems.
results_summary: The paper proposes FastAdjust, a method for incrementally updating KNN graphs after embedding model fine-tuning rather than performing full reconstruction. It uses product quantization-based clustering to narrow the candidate neighbor search space and adaptively allocates update resources according to data density and embedding variation magnitude. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that FastAdjust adapts KNN graphs to embedding updates with significantly reduced computational cost while maintaining graph quality. The method shows strong practical value and scalability for scenarios where embeddings are periodically updated.
limitations: FastAdjust only supports updating KNN graphs before and after embedding model fine-tuning; Cannot directly adapt to scenarios of greatly updating or replacing the embedding model; Application scenarios supported by FastAdjust are still limited
research_gaps: Providing support for other vector indexes beyond KNN graphs; Developing processing strategies for large fine-tuning amplitude where neighbor relationships have completely changed; Handling scenarios where the embedding model is directly replaced by another model; Combining more adaptive resource allocation strategies; Automatically determining hyperparameters for the various optimization methods proposed

title: Enhancing Graph-based Approximate Maximum Inner Product Search via Norm-Adaptive Partitioning
relevance_reason: The paper is directly about core vector database technology: it proposes a new indexing method (NAP) and hybrid index (HT-NSW) specifically for Approximate Maximum Inner Product Search, a fundamental operation in vector databases, and analyzes the theoretical limitations of graph-based indexing for MIPS.
research_focus: The paper addresses the norm bias problem in graph-based Approximate Maximum Inner Product Search (AMIPS) and proposes a Norm-Adaptive Partitioning (NAP) framework to mitigate the norm domination phenomenon that degrades proximity graph performance for MIPS.
method: The paper theoretically analyzes norm domination in MIPS, proposes NAP to partition vectors into Head (large-norm, exhaustive search), Body (moderate-norm, proximity graph), and Tail (small-norm, pruned) segments, designs a practical partitioning algorithm using the Elbow method, and introduces a hybrid index HT-NSW combining a hash table for Head and a proximity graph (NSW) for Body.
indexing_methods: LSH; APG (Approximate Proximity Graph); NSW; hash table
application_domain: Vector databases, large-scale data retrieval, information retrieval, and recommendation systems
results_summary: The paper identifies and quantifies the norm domination phenomenon, showing that over 99% of top-10 MIPS results in skewed datasets originate from the top 0.05% of large-norm vectors. Building on this, the proposed NAP framework partitions data into Head, Body, and Tail segments with tailored search strategies. The resulting hybrid index HT-NSW reduces the index size of existing proximity graphs by over 50% and achieves more than 2x query speedup over state-of-the-art graph-based AMIPS methods at the same recall level. Experimental validation on datasets including MNIST, Gist, Tiny5M, Audio, and YahooMusic confirms the effectiveness of the approach, particularly when datasets exhibit wide norm distributions.
research_gaps: Improve the structure of HT-NSW based on the data distribution; Develop efficient index maintenance for HT-NSW to make it suitable for modern vector databases

title: LlymX: Multimodal LLM-Augmented XR for Context-Aware Information Access
relevance_reason: Vector databases are mentioned only as a component of the RAG pipeline in the LlymX prototype; the paper's main subject is XR-LLM interaction design for industrial information access, not vector database technology itself.
research_focus: Design and evaluation of LlymX, a prototype combining Extended Reality (XR) with LLM-driven retrieval-augmented generation for context-aware, hands-free information access in industrial environments.
method: A Unity-based 3D environment is combined with an LLM-driven backend using RAG and vector databases. Spatial user actions (gestures, object selection) are grounded in semantic object representations and linked to retrieval from a structured knowledge base. A user study compares LlymX against menu-based and infographic-based XR interfaces on usability (SUS), task completion time, and cognitive workload.
application_domain: Industrial environments: technical information access for complex equipment and 3D models, with potential extensions to education and healthcare.
results_summary: The paper presents the LlymX prototype and evaluates it through a user study comparing three interaction modalities (menu-based, infographic-based, LLM-based). The LLM-based modality was found to be significantly more usable (SUS) than static infographics and comparable to traditional menus. Task completion time and cognitive workload showed no statistically significant differences across modalities. Participants appreciated the flexibility of conversational interaction and the hands-free capability. The authors conclude that LLM-based agents enhance flexibility and perceived usability but only when embedded within well-structured interaction flows.
limitations: Currently implemented as a proof-of-concept rather than a fully deployed system; Requires 3D models to be accompanied by descriptive metadata; Relies on the availability of an up-to-date, structured knowledge base; Raises ethical and safety considerations for safety-critical industrial or healthcare tasks; Outputs must remain grounded in validated and up-to-date knowledge sources with clear provenance
research_gaps: Further validation and refinement in realistic industrial settings; Clarifying when and how LLM-powered XR systems can effectively support next-generation intelligent environments; Extension into other domains such as education and healthcare; Development of hybrid models integrating conversational AI and traditional UI elements for greater practical effectiveness

title: VecCard: a learned cardinality estimator for predicate filtering queries on vector databases
relevance_reason: The paper proposes a learned cardinality estimation model specifically designed for vector database query optimization, addressing challenges unique to vector databases (hybrid queries, ANNS + predicate filtering, graph-based indexes), and is evaluated on a vector database system (DingoDB). However, the main subject is the ML-based estimation technique rather than vector databases as a whole, making it a substantial but not sole focus.
research_focus: Accurate cardinality estimation for complex predicate filtering queries in vector databases, specifically for hybrid queries combining scalar metadata filtering with approximate nearest neighbor search, to improve query plan selection in vector database optimizers.
method: A Tree-LSTM-based architecture that encodes the hierarchical structure of nested Boolean predicates (AST alignment) combined with a domain-aware metadata and predicate encoding scheme, augmented with an Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) based incremental learning mechanism to adapt to evolving data distributions without full retraining.
application_domain: Vector database query optimization for hybrid queries (predicate filtering + ANNS), with applications in semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, and recommendation.
results_summary: VecCard was evaluated on two real-world datasets (MOOCCubeX and Yelp) integrated into the DingoDB vector database. It achieved a Mean Q-Error of 1.91 and Median Q-Error of 1.29 on Yelp, representing a 70% reduction in average error compared to the strongest structural baseline (TreeRNN). On the sparser MOOCCubeX dataset, VecCard maintained a stable Mean Q-Error of 5.77 while traditional estimators degraded to errors in the tens or hundreds. When integrated into DingoDB's native optimizer, VecCard significantly reduced query latency and resource consumption across heterogeneous index structures such as HNSW and IVF_FLAT. The EWC-based incremental learning mechanism enabled adaptation to distribution shifts without catastrophic forgetting.
research_gaps: Extending VecCard to support complex multi-table join scenarios in enterprise-level multimodal databases; Transitioning from pure cardinality estimation to end-to-end cost model learning that directly predicts nonlinear hardware execution costs for traversing vector graph indexes; Exploring federated learning paradigms for cardinality estimation in distributed vector databases to address privacy-sensitive AI applications

title: BAGS: A Bit-Partitioned Quantization-Aware Architecture for Accelerating Graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is the core technology of vector databases—approximate nearest neighbor search—proposing a new hardware architecture to accelerate HNSW-based search and benchmarking it against existing ANNS systems. Vector indexing and similarity search are the central focus, not merely a tool used for another purpose.
research_focus: Accelerating graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (specifically HNSW) by addressing the memory-bandwidth bottleneck through a software-hardware co-optimized architecture that combines scalar quantization with re-ranking while preserving full-precision accuracy.
method: A bit-partitioned vector search framework using 8-bit partitioned quantization applied to both graph traversal and re-ranking phases, combined with a unified hardware accelerator that shares computational resources across both phases and a redesigned memory data layout to minimize hardware and memory overhead.
indexing_methods: HNSW; Product Quantization (PQ); Scalar Quantization (SQ); bit-partitioned quantization
application_domain: Recommendation systems, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), search engines, and natural language processing
results_summary: The paper proposes BAGS, a software-hardware co-optimized architecture that applies 8-bit partitioned quantization in both the HNSW graph traversal and re-ranking phases to alleviate memory bandwidth saturation. A unified hardware accelerator supports both phases with shared computational resources, and a redesigned memory data layout reduces storage overhead. Experimental results show BAGS achieves 63.4×, 12.9×, and 1.6× speedups over CPU, GPU, and state-of-the-art ASIC-based accelerator baselines respectively, while incurring minimal hardware implementation overhead. The approach preserves full-precision accuracy without requiring separate processing units for quantized and full-precision computations.

title: Versatile Sketch-Based Attribute Filtering for Hybrid Vector Search
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is vector database core technology: it proposes a new hybrid vector search technique built on HNSW graphs, compares it against existing ANN indexing methods (PQ, LSH, IVF, PG-based), and evaluates query processing performance for combined similarity and predicate filtering.
research_focus: Efficient processing of hybrid vector search queries that combine approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) retrieval with predicate filtering on structured data attributes, specifically proposing a metadata-agnostic, popularity-aware approach using proximity graph structures.
method: The approach constructs clusters from the base layer of HNSW graphs and maintains in-memory sketches (count-min sketch for point queries, CDF-based regression model for range filtering) populated with attribute values from nodes. During search, the nearest neighbor of the query vector is identified, and a two-hop search is conditionally triggered based on the popularity of the specific predicate within the corresponding cluster.
indexing_methods: HNSW; Product Quantization (PQ); Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH); Inverted File Index (IVF); Proximity Graph (PG)-based approaches; Count-Min Sketch; CDF-based regression model
application_domain: General-purpose hybrid vector search combining semantic similarity retrieval with structured attribute filtering (illustrated with a medical X-ray scan example)
results_summary: The paper proposes a popularity-aware hybrid vector search solution that uses HNSW base-layer clusters with in-memory sketches to decide whether to perform a two-hop search based on predicate popularity. Experiments on five real-world datasets, focusing on low-selectivity queries where pre-filtering is inefficient, show that the proposed approach outperforms alternative PG-based and other ANN-based methods. The solution also demonstrates greater robustness compared to existing techniques. The method remains metadata-agnostic, avoiding the need for separate graph structures per attribute or modifications to the original graph.
